findings.title: Update invalidation is skipped for org-linked IDPs whose organization is disabled, leaving stale login caches
findings.description:
`update()` passes `getById(...)` as `original` (line 91). With the organization feature on, that is the wrapper from `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (lines 432-446), whose `isEnabled()` is false when the organization or realm-level organizations are disabled. The cached ID sets, by contrast, come from the JPA query, which filters on the raw `enabled` column only. So the invalidation decision and the cache contents use different definitions of "enabled".

Failure sequence:
1. A public, enabled IDP X is linked to an org and its ID is in the `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL` login caches.
2. The org is disabled. Nothing invalidates the login keys: `InfinispanOrganizationProvider.registerOrganizationInvalidation` (lines 300-308) only touches the org id, `cacheKeyOrgId` and domain keys.
3. An admin updates X to `hideOnLogin=true`, `linkOnly=true`, or `kc.org.broker.public=false`.
4. `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` is false (wrapper reports disabled) and `test(updated)` is false, so line 405 returns without invalidating.
5. The org is re-enabled (again no login-cache invalidation).
6. `getForLogin` serves X from the cached ID set. `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` (lines 75, 80) re-checks only `isEnabled()`, so a hidden, link-only or non-public broker appears on the login page until some unrelated change invalidates the key.

A second gap in the same method: toggling `BROKER_PUBLIC` on an IDP not linked to any org skips invalidation at lines 409-411 (predicate true before and after, `organizationId` null on both sides). The delegate result for `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL` with a null organization does change, because the default `getForLogin` (`IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:173-181`) filters only on `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` and does not require an organization link.

Suggested fix: evaluate the predicate against the raw stored state (e.g. `idpDelegate.getById`, as `remove()` already does with `idpDelegate.getByAlias`) and include the `BROKER_PUBLIC` value in the "unchanged" comparison. Alternatively, have the consumer re-apply the full login predicate rather than only `isEnabled()`.

findings.title: Test cleanup targets a non-existent alias, so the created IDPs leak into the shared realm
findings.description:
Both cleanup registrations (line 381 inside the loop, and again around line 425 for `idp-alias-20`) use `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`. No IDP has the literal alias `"alias"`; they should be `"idp-alias-" + i` and `"idp-alias-20"`. `TestCleanup.addCleanup` swallows every exception (`TestCleanup.java:65-72`), so the resulting 404 is silent and all the IDPs survive the test. The test realm is not re-imported per method (`AbstractKeycloakTest.isImportAfterEachMethod()` returns false).

This was copied from the same mistake in `testCacheIDPByOrg` (line 303). The new test asserts exact counts (5 / 5 / 10, then 6 / 5 / 11, then 5 / 6 / 11), so leftover login-eligible IDPs from another test in the class can make it order-dependent.

findings.title: Test coverage misses invalidation-critical paths and asserts only cache internals
`getForLogin` duplicates `getByOrganization` almost line for line
findings.description:
Lines 214-255 repeat the list-query caching algorithm of lines 168-211: invalid check, load or extend `IdentityProviderListQuery`, resolve IDs through `getById`, fall back to the delegate on a miss. Only the cache key, search key and delegate call differ. A private helper taking the key, search key and a `Supplier<Stream<IdentityProviderModel>>` would remove about 40 duplicated lines of revision-sensitive logic.

Smaller duplication in the same change:
- the `for (FetchMode mode : FetchMode.values()) registerInvalidation(...)` loop appears at both 385-387 and 415-417;
- `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` builds and evaluates `getLoginPredicate()` up to four times (lines 405, 409) instead of computing two booleans once.

findings.title: `getLoginPredicate()` contract changed in the public SPI without documentation
findings.description:
The predicate now also requires org-linked IDPs to have `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`. That condition is not one of the `LoginFilter` enum values, so `getLoginPredicate()` and `getLoginSearchOptions()` no longer describe the same rule. The enum Javadoc ("contains all fields that are considered…", line 216) and the `getForLogin` Javadoc are unchanged, and the method itself has no Javadoc.

The change also affects an existing caller: `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` (`IdentityProviderBean.java:225-227`) will now filter out non-public org-linked IDPs for users with linked federated identities. In `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` (lines 86-97) the new clause partly duplicates the existing org check.

findings.title: `remove()` now always hits the database, and the null-IDP path is still unguarded
findings.description:
`idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` now runs unconditionally at line 100, where it previously ran only when the alias key was invalidated; the JPA `remove` then loads the same entity again. The comment at line 102 ("lookup idp by alias in cache…") no longer describes the code.

If the alias does not exist, `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(null)` is safe thanks to the `Objects::nonNull` guard. But `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` at line 103 still throws a NullPointerException when the key is invalid. That behaviour predates this change; now that `storedIdp` is in hand, an early `if (storedIdp == null) return false;` would close it.

findings.title: Login cache granularity is coarse for realms with many organizations
findings.description: Each `FetchMode` has a single cache entry holding a map of organization id to IDP IDs. The first lookup for every new organization invalidates the whole entry and re-adds a copy of the full map (lines 236-240). Any login-relevant IDP change in the realm drops all three entries for all organizations. A cache hit still costs one `getById` per IDP (lines 245-252). This matches the existing `getByOrganization` design, but it now sits on the login-page hot path.

findings.title: Consumer has to compensate for provider semantics
findings.description: The added `idp.isEnabled()` re-check is duplicated on lines 75 and 80, and is needed because `getForLogin` can return models whose org-aware `isEnabled()` is false. That makes "returns IDPs available for login" untrue for the caching provider, and every other caller must know to re-filter. Applying the filter inside `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` would keep the contract in one place.

findings.title: Direct invalidation on create, remove and organization link/unlink
findings.description: `create` and `remove` register invalidation for all `FetchMode` keys when the IDP qualifies for login, and `remove` evaluates the predicate against the raw stored model. Organization link/unlink and organization removal go through `session.identityProviders().update(...)` (`JpaOrganizationProvider.java:141, 341-342, 368-371`), so they reach the `organizationId` comparison and invalidate correctly. The cache key and revision handling match the established `getByOrganization` pattern.
